summary: No verifiable fresh signal today. Every free-source result repeated the 1 July NSW reform package already captured across the 28 June - 15 August digests: the psychological-injury 'relevant event' compensability test requiring a real and direct connection to employment with employment as the main contributing factor; the staged Whole Person Impairment thresholds (25% from 1 July 2026, rising in later years) with a partial ongoing-payment band for 21-24% impairment; the 130-week cap on weekly payments for primary psychological injury; the fixed employer excess applying to policies issued or renewed from 30 June 2026; and the 2026-27 icare premium settings holding Workers Compensation Industry Classification rates flat, the minimum premium at $240, and reducing experience-rated premium-increase capping from 30% to 25%. No new NSW regulator or tribunal release surfaced in the last 24 hours: no fresh Personal Injury Commission decision, Industrial Relations Commission 'relevant conduct' determination, SafeWork NSW prosecution or IRO release appeared. SafeWork NSW's largest-ever inspector uplift and its August psychosocial inspection campaign trace to the March 2026 announcement and remain documented context, not a new signal.
